clue.text: Tasty paste from West Asia used all round Britain

indicators.note: all round tells us the rearranged Asia letters go around another piece
used here in the sense of worn or knocked about, so the letters of Asia are rearranged

explanation.surface: A condiment from West Asia that has spread across Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' signals an anagram of ASIA, giving ASAI, which goes 'all round' B to make ASABI after W.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasabi is the hot green Japanese horseradish condiment served with sushi, a pungent paste.

clue.text: Helium in water changing climate

indicators.note: changing shows the letters of the pieces are being altered into a new order

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium
taken as written

explanation.surface: A science note about helium dissolving in water as the climate shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather is the state of the atmosphere, loosely the same as climate in everyday speech.

clue.text: Small vegetable is shiny

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a leek is an onion-family vegetable

explanation.surface: A greengrocer praises a little vegetable for its gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek describes a smooth glossy surface, as of well-groomed hair or fur.

clue.text: Bird damaged on a road

parts.note: bust is informal for broken or damaged

explanation.surface: A bird has been hurt on a road, perhaps by a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged on a road' looks like an anagram of ON A ROAD, but 'damaged' is BUST.
explanation.definitionFit: The bustard is a large heavy ground-dwelling bird of open plains.

clue.text: Penny finished with favourite doll

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny in British money
up can mean finished, as in time is up
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A child has spent their last penny on a beloved doll.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet is a figure or doll moved by strings or a hand inside it.

clue.text: Increased shame is difficult to control

parts.note: up means increased, as when prices are up
a shame means a pity, as in what a shame

explanation.surface: Growing embarrassment proves hard to keep in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity means arrogant and self-important, refusing to know one's place, so hard to manage.

clue.text: Champion rugby player working at hospital department

parts.note: a prop is a forward in the front row of a rugby scrum
on means working, as a machine that is switched on
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A star rugby player is doing a shift in a hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' reads as a title for the player but is the definition, used as a noun for a supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion of a cause is a proponent, someone who argues for and supports it.

clue.text: Label meat cooked for partners in the ring

parts.note: a tag is a label tied on something

indicators.note: cooked suggests something tampered with, so the letters of meat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction: label the meat once it has been cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag team is a pair of wrestlers who take turns fighting in the ring.

clue.text: Depressed setter with gin drunk in No 10?

parts.note: down means depressed or low in spirits

indicators.note: drunk suggests a wild jumble, so the letters of setter and gin are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy crossword setter getting drunk on gin at the Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' and 'gin' are rearranged by 'drunk' to give INGSTREET.
explanation.definitionFit: Number 10 Downing Street is the official London residence of the British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Juliet with nausea spewed over bag for writer

parts.note: Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: spewed means thrown out messily, so the letters of nausea are scrambled
over means turned over, so the word for bag is read backwards

parts.note: to bag is to net, catch

explanation.surface: Juliet feels sick and throws up over a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spewed' rearranges NAUSEA to ANEAUS; 'over' turns NET into TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen was the English novelist who wrote Pride and Prejudice and Emma.

clue.text: Winter vehicle currently parking in Berkshire town

indicators.note: in tells us these pieces are placed within the town's name

parts.note: Slough is a town in Berkshire, a county west of London
now means currently, at present
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: A gritting truck is currently parked somewhere in a Berkshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowplough is a vehicle fitted with a blade for clearing snow from roads in winter.

clue.text: Pitch declared first-class for part of match

indicators.note: declared means spoken out, so we want a word that sounds like the throwing word

parts.note: to pitch a ball is to chuck it
A, as in A1 or grade A, means first-class

explanation.surface: A cricket pitch has been declared top quality for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' and 'declared' suggest cricket, but the match is polo.
explanation.definitionFit: A chukka is one of the timed periods into which a polo match is divided.

clue.text: Gas put a tiny bit of taste into negroni cocktail

indicators.note: put into tells us one piece goes inside the other
a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of negroni are mixed up
a tiny bit of a word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A bartender adds a hint of flavour to a negroni cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' rearranges NEGRONI to NIROGEN, and 'into' places T from 'a tiny bit of taste' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is a colourless gas forming most of the air we breathe.

clue.text: Syrup mixed in drink in garden awfully popular at the end of June

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters of garden are rearranged

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A drink served at a garden party in June proves terribly popular.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a sweet red pomegranate syrup added to cocktails and soft drinks.

clue.text: Gymnasts upset about source of unusual eye movements

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other
upset means overturned, so the letters of gymnasts are thrown into a new order
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Gymnasts are upset by what is causing their odd eye movements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges GYMNASTS into NYSTAGMS, and 'about' puts it around U.
explanation.definitionFit: Nystagmus is the medical term for involuntary rapid oscillation of the eyes.

clue.text: Sailor leaving American navy joint

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so those letters are dropped from the sailor

parts.note: a seaman is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor quits the American navy and heads for a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like a dive bar in the surface but means a join.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is the line where two pieces of material are joined together.

clue.text: Find out about American saints

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: US means American

explanation.surface: Someone researching the lives of American saints.
explanation.definitionFit: To suss something is informal for to work it out or discover the truth.

clue.text: Bone with small top joined to bone with no name

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so that letter is taken out of the bone

parts.note: the ulna is a bone of the forearm

explanation.surface: An anatomist describes a bone with a small cap fused to an unnamed bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The scapula is the anatomical name for the shoulder blade, a flat bone.

clue.text: When sister gets to beat backside of current helper?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: the backside of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A sister is allowed to spank the bottom of the present helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is someone employed to help another with their work.

clue.text: Eager trainee losing end of decider on points

indicators.note: losing means dropping a letter from the trainee

parts.note: an intern is a trainee working to gain experience

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: A keen trainee loses at the end of a deciding match on points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing end of decider' removes R from INTERN to leave INTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense describes someone earnest and passionate, highly keen about something.

clue.text: Mounted police meeting a member about going from place to place

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means going up, so the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
AM is an Assembly Member of the Welsh parliament
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Mounted police meet a politician on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' turns CIDAMON upwards. 'Mounted police' looks like a single phrase, but 'Mounted' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic describes people who wander from place to place without a fixed home.

clue.text: Go round base of col in rocky ridge

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other
rocky means shaky or unstable, so the letters of ridge are rearranged
in a down clue the base of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A walker skirts the foot of a mountain pass on a rocky ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' rearranges RIDGE to GIRDE, and 'in' places L from 'base of col' within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To girdle is to encircle or surround something, as a belt does a waist.

clue.text: Vicar with ale brewed for royalist supporter

indicators.note: brewed means concocted, so the letters are mixed afresh

explanation.surface: A vicar and a pint of ale, brewed for a loyal monarchist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavaliers were supporters of King Charles I in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Ukip leader entering vehicle getting a shock

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so that letter goes into the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails in a street

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The Ukip leader gets on a tram and receives a jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Ukip is the UK Independence Party, a British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is a severe emotional or physical shock.

clue.text: Graduate set up software program for religious leader

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means raised, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
a bot is an automated software program

explanation.surface: A graduate has set up a computer program for a church leader.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the head of a monastery of monks.

clue.text: Cantankerous old person who's against burying muck in drive

indicators.note: burying means hiding inside, so the other pieces go into the word for against

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside another

parts.note: urge means drive, an impulse
mud is muck

explanation.surface: A grumpy old person complains about muck trodden into the driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: 'in' works inside 'burying', so the drive word holds the muck before the against word wraps around both.
explanation.definitionFit: A curmudgeon is a bad-tempered, grumbling person, often elderly.

clue.text: Lad clutching top of designer group

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so the boy surrounds the other letter

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A lad grips the top designed by someone famous.
explanation.definitionFit: A body is a group of people acting together, such as a governing body.

clue.text: See 9
Rotten secretary hiding introduction to promissory note

indicators.note: hiding means concealing inside, so these pieces go into the secretary
an introduction to a word is its first letter

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A dishonest secretary is concealing an IOU.
explanation.definitionFit: Septic means infected and putrefying, as a wound gone bad.
